desc:
Along a road there are n posts in a row, and installing a lamp at post i costs costs[i]. The road is inspected in every stretch of w consecutive posts (posts s, s + 1, ..., s + w - 1 for each valid start s), and every such stretch must contain at least one lamp.

Return the minimum total cost of the lamps. For example, for costs = [4, 2, 6, 1, 5] and w = 3 the answer is 3 (lamps at posts 1 and 3). With w = 1 every post needs a lamp.

Equivalently: choose which posts to leave dark so that no w consecutive posts are all dark, while the lit ones cost as little as possible.
hints: Define the state as 'the last lamp is at post i'. Which earlier lamp positions may precede it without leaving an uncovered stretch of w posts in between?
If the previous lamp is at post j < i, the posts j+1..i-1 are dark, so i - j - 1 ≤ w - 1, i.e. j ≥ i - w. The first lamp must be at post w-1 or earlier, and the last lamp at post n-w or later.
dp[i] = costs[i] + min(dp[j] for j in [i-w, i-1]), with a virtual lamp at position -1 of cost 0. That is a sliding window minimum, so a monotonic deque brings the total work to O(n).
editorial: Let dp[i] be the cheapest way to cover the prefix with the last lamp placed at post i. The gap between consecutive lamps (and between the road start and the first lamp) may hold at most w - 1 dark posts, otherwise some stretch of w posts would contain no lamp. Hence dp[i] = costs[i] + min(dp[j]) over earlier lamps j with i - w ≤ j ≤ i - 1, where a virtual lamp at index -1 with cost 0 represents 'no lamp yet' and is allowed for i ≤ w - 1.

At the end the last lamp must leave at most w - 1 dark posts after it, so the answer is the minimum of dp[j] over j ≥ n - w. Evaluating each dp value by scanning w predecessors costs O(n · w), which is too slow for the maximum input; the minimum over a window that slides one step at a time is maintained with a monotonic deque of increasing dp values, giving O(n) total. For w = 2 this reduces to the cheapest set of lamps with no two neighbouring dark posts.
